public_rationale: Read plainly, the claim is that image generators in 2025 are far better than in 2022, and that a sharp rider on a correct, spoked, pedalled wheel was beyond what 2022 tools reliably produced. A CyclingTips test in August 2022 tried five popular tools on cycling prompts and judged most of the realistic images 'a pretty decisive no' for use. On the GenEval benchmark, which checks whether images get objects and counts right, Stable Diffusion v1.5 (a 2022 model) scores 0.43. GPT-4o, the 2025 generator behind ChatGPT images, scores 0.84, roughly double. Together these support the claim of vast improvement. The absolute 'no model could' cannot be proven literally, and some 2022 outputs were good, so this verdict depends on reading it as ordinary emphasis.
limitations: The verdict depends on reading 'no model could have done this' as emphasis rather than a literal universal negative.
The specific ChatGPT-5 image in the post was not inspected.
The benchmark measures prompt accuracy, not visual sharpness.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: AI image generation in mid-2025 is much better than in 2022. The 2022 tools generally could not produce a clean, sharp picture of a person on a correctly built wheel with spokes and pedals.

The absolute 'no model could' is read as ordinary emphasis that this was beyond what 2022 tools reliably did. It is not read as a literal claim that no single 2022 sample could ever have looked like this.
The period runs from 2022 to the post date, because the claim compares the two.
criteria.support_condition: Sources showing that 2022 image tools mostly produced mangled or unusable bicycle and rider images, and that 2025 systems score far higher on measures of image quality or prompt accuracy.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Documented 2022 outputs or benchmarks showing that 2022 models routinely produced sharp, mechanically correct images of riders on cycles, or showing no large quality gap between 2022 and 2025 models.
